title: Zeraki Alternatives in Kenya: 7 Best School Systems (2026)
h1: Zeraki Alternatives in Kenya: 7 Best School Management Systems (2026)
description: Looking for a Zeraki alternative in Kenya? Compare 7 school management systems on M-Pesa, WhatsApp messaging, CBC reports, pricing and support.
author: SQUL Team
intro: If you are already using Zeraki — or comparing it — and wondering what else is out there, this is for you. Below are seven **Zeraki alternatives in Kenya**, compared on the things schools actually feel: automatic M-Pesa reconciliation, WhatsApp and SMS parent messaging, CBC report cards, time to go live, and support. For the wider field, see the [best school management software in Kenya](/blog/best-school-management-software-kenya).
We will not pretend all seven are equally good, and we will be clear about the case where staying on Zeraki is the right call. The goal is a shortlist you can demo in a week.
quickAnswer: Editor's note: competitor features and pricing change and are described here at a high level from public information. Verify current details with each vendor before you buy. SQUL figures are our own. Last reviewed September 2026.

sections.heading: Why schools look for a Zeraki alternative

blocks.text: Zeraki is well known in Kenyan secondary schools, especially for exam analytics and reporting. Schools start looking elsewhere for reasons that are usually operational rather than academic:

items: **Fees still take too long to reconcile.** If M-Pesa payments must be matched by hand, the bursar's first two weeks of term are still manual.
**Parent messaging is SMS-only.** Parents who live in WhatsApp are harder to reach, and reminders are less effective.
**The office wants one system.** Juggling an analytics tool plus spreadsheets plus an SMS service means data that does not agree with itself.
**Onboarding or cost feels heavy.** Some schools want to start small, on a free term, and prove value before committing.

sections.heading: What to compare before you switch

blocks.text: Score every alternative on the same seven points, weighted to your own pain:

rows: Does it match Paybill/till payments to the right learner, or import a statement?
Can you reach parents on both channels from one place?
Printable term report cards without retyping marks.
Rosters published instantly; same-day parent alerts.
Can you collect fees this term, not next year?
Who answers on reporting day? Role-based access? Backups?

blocks.caption: At a glance. Confirm each vendor's current capabilities directly.

blocks.text: SQUL is built for the operational reality of a Kenyan school office. Where Zeraki is strongest on analytics, SQUL is strongest on the two jobs that decide a term: reconciling fees and reaching parents.

items: **Automatic M-Pesa reconciliation (Daraja)** — Paybill and till payments matched to the right learner, balances and receipts updated the same day.
**WhatsApp and SMS** — reminders, absence alerts and exam notices on both channels from one place.
**CBC and 8-4-4 report cards** — captured once, printed ready.
**Timetables, duty rosters, and same-day attendance alerts.**
**Multi-campus** with consolidated reports, and a **free term** to start.

blocks.text: If you want the direct head-to-head, read [SQUL vs Zeraki](/blog/squl-vs-zeraki).

items: **EdAdmin** — mature and feature-deep, often chosen by larger or more established institutions; onboarding and cost can be heavy for a small school.
**SchoolMaster** — leans accounting-first, good for bursars who think in ledgers; lighter on parent communication.
**Fedena** — a broad global ERP for groups and colleges; not Kenyan-first, so no native M-Pesa or WhatsApp.
**OpenSIS** — open-source and customisable for schools with in-house IT; you own the servers, security and training.
**Custom builds** — tailored to one school, but high cost, maintenance risk, and a single point of failure.
**Excel + WhatsApp** — the familiar baseline; cheap to start, expensive in bursar hours every single day.

blocks.caption: Whatever you choose, the test is the same: does it reduce work for the office, or just move it around?

sections.heading: When staying on Zeraki is the right choice

blocks.text: Be honest with yourself. Zeraki may still be the right fit if:

items: Your dominant need is **exam analytics and performance reporting**, and that is working well for you.
Your **fees and parent messaging are already handled** by another tool you are happy with.
Your **staff are trained and invested** in the current workflows, and switching costs outweigh the gains.

faqs.question: What is the best Zeraki alternative in Kenya?
faqs.answer: For most Kenyan schools, SQUL is the strongest alternative because it focuses on automatic M-Pesa reconciliation and WhatsApp plus SMS parent messaging, which Zeraki does not centre on. EdAdmin and SchoolMaster are other options for different priorities.

faqs.question: Does SQUL do everything Zeraki does?
faqs.answer: Both cover CBC/8-4-4 report cards and timetables. SQUL leads on automatic M-Pesa and WhatsApp/SMS; Zeraki leads on exam analytics and league tables. Choose based on which matters more to your school.

faqs.question: How hard is it to move from Zeraki to another system?
faqs.answer: Most schools import their learner list and link guardian phone numbers, then start collecting fees within about two weeks. The main work is data, not downtime.

faqs.question: Are there free school management systems in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Yes — open-source options like OpenSIS are free to license but cost in IT staff and training. SQUL offers a free term so you can prove value before paying.

faqs.question: Will switching disrupt a term?
faqs.answer: Not if you schedule it before opening day. Start on a free term, import learners, and go live for fee collection in the first two weeks.

faqs.question: Can I keep using Zeraki for analytics and add SQUL?
faqs.answer: Some schools do run both, but most prefer one system so records agree. SQUL covers CBC and 8-4-4 report cards, so it can often replace a separate analytics tool.
